logline: A villager kid wakes to a torch on every block of his village and is sure a party is coming, but the last growing row leads to his own door, where his best friend, the village's only player, sets down the torch he walked him home with every night, waves, and walks away without 'see you tomorrow'.
question: why tf did someone put 6,000 torches on this village overnight?
premise: One morning a plains village wakes with a torch on every grass block, fence post, roof ridge and hay bale: six thousand of them, when one torch lights a whole house. The baby villager who tells it is thrilled: something big must be coming, like a party. Jonah, the village's only player and the kid's best friend, walks him home with his torch every night, so the kid is never in the dark, and says 'see you tomorrow'. This morning all of Jonah's things are in the kid's family chest (presents for the party!) and Jonah's house is gone (he's moving in with us!). One row is still growing; the kid follows it to his own door.
twist: Nothing is coming: Jonah is going. He is leaving the game for good and can't walk his friend home any more, so he spent his last night lighting every block of the village so his friend is never in the dark (the gesture, in the kid's own words at the door, L13: 'So I'm NEVER in the DARK!'; nothing claims mobs stop spawning). He took his house down and gave everything he owned to the kid's family. His own torch, the one he walked the kid home with, is the last one: he places it at the kid's door, waves, and walks away, and this time he doesn't say 'see you tomorrow'. The kid thinks he forgot.

lines.text: SOMEONE put / six THOUSAND / TORCHES / on my VILLAGE / last NIGHT.

lines.direction: one breath, amazed and delighted, a lift on the number

lines.text: FENCES. / ROOFS. / HAY bales. / Not ONE / DARK block.
lines.say: Fences. Roofs. Hay bales. Not one dark BLOCK.
lines.direction: a fast happy list, then the topper

lines.text: ONE torch / LIGHTS / a whole HOUSE. / So WHY / six THOUSAND?
lines.say: One torch lights a whole house. So why six THOUSAND?
lines.direction: proud of knowing it, then delighted puzzling

lines.text: Something BIG / must be COMING! / Like a PARTY!
lines.say: Something big must be coming! Like a PARTY!
lines.direction: delighted, bouncing, full volume; never scared

lines.text: Our VILLAGE / has one PLAYER. / JONAH. / My best FRIEND.
lines.say: Our village has one player. Jonah. My best FRIEND.
lines.direction: proud, a grin on the name

lines.text: Every NIGHT, / he WALKS me / HOME / with his TORCH.
lines.say: Every night, he walks me home with his TORCH.
lines.direction: fond and quick, happy about it

lines.text: This MORNING, / I FOUND / his STUFF / in OUR chest.
lines.say: This morning, I found his stuff in our CHEST.
lines.direction: excited, a lift at the end

lines.text: And his HOUSE? / GONE. / He's MOVING / in with US!
lines.say: And his house? Gone. He's moving in with US!
lines.direction: puzzled for a beat, then overjoyed

lines.text: One ROW / of TORCHES / was still GROWING. / I HAD / to see WHO.
lines.say: One row of torches was still growing. I had to see WHO.

lines.text: I FOLLOWED it / to MY door.
lines.say: I followed it to my DOOR.

lines.text: It was JONAH! / With his LAST torch. / So I'm NEVER / in the DARK!
lines.say: It was Jonah! With his last torch. So I'm never in the DARK!
